rationale:
bugs_open/424 round 2. The bugfix_420_417 lane ran live dynamic testing of the already-approved-and-deployed keyed-ground matting fix and found a real defect in the fail-closed guard: MatteStats.BorderKeyed was computed from BFS flood-fill REACHABILITY (was a border pixel within `outer` distance of the key colour?), not from the pixel's FINAL alpha after grading. Its own doc comment always said 'the fraction of border pixels that ended up fully transparent' -- the code never matched that. Consequence, measured live: a genuine 0.0%-actually-transparent FAILURE (the model ignored the key colour) and an 87.4%-actually-transparent SUCCESS both read BorderKeyed=1.000, because both had every border pixel reachable within `outer` even though the failure case's pixels never got close enough to `inner` to reach alpha 0. The fail-closed guard in dynamic_adapter.go (unchanged by this fix -- it always checked BorderKeyed >= 0.95 correctly) was therefore being fed the wrong number and could not distinguish a real failure from a real success.

Verified against the actual code before fixing (not taken on the reporting session's word alone): read keyground.go, confirmed keyedByBorder (reachability) feeds stats.BorderKeyed directly with no reference to final alpha.

Fix: track each pixel's FINAL alpha through the existing grading pass into a new finalAlpha array, and compute the border stat from that (alpha==0) instead of from BFS reachability. No change to the BFS pass itself, no change to the fail-closed threshold check in dynamic_adapter.go -- only what number feeds it.

New test TestKeyOutBackground_GradedBorderIsNotBorderKeyed reproduces the exact reported shape (a uniform border colour placed mid-graded-band: reachable, never close enough to `inner`). Mutation-proven this session: temporarily reinstated the pre-fix computation in the working tree, ran the new test, confirmed it FAILS (reports BorderKeyed=1.000 as the live report described), then restored the fix (not committed in that state -- git stash is banned on this tree, so the revert/restore went through Edit on the tracked file directly, verified via `go test` before and after).

plan.summary: The keyed-ground matte's fail-closed guard statistic (BorderKeyed) was computed from flood-fill reachability instead of final pixel alpha, so it could not distinguish a real 0%-transparent failure from a real 87%-transparent success -- found by live dynamic testing after the previous round's approval. Fixed to compute the stat from what the pixels actually became, matching its own doc comment; mutation-proven against the pre-fix code.

edits.rationale: Replace the border-stat computation's data source: track finalAlpha per pixel through the existing grading switch (already computed for the output image; this just also records it into a parallel array), then compute BorderKeyed as the fraction of border-ring pixels with finalAlpha==0. Removes the old computation that used keyedByBorder (BFS reachability) directly. No change to the flood-fill algorithm, the enclosed-hole pass, or despill -- only the border statistic's arithmetic.

New regression test reproducing the exact live-reported failure shape: a uniform border colour at a distance strictly between inner and outer (reachable, never transparent). Asserts BorderKeyed reads near 0 (post-fix) rather than 1.0 (pre-fix, matching the live measurement). Mutation-proven against the actual reinstated pre-fix code this session, not merely written to pass against the fix.

+// ACTUAL alpha stayed well above 0, used to report BorderKeyed=1.000 despite

+// 0.0%-actually-transparent failure and an 87.4%-actually-transparent success

+func TestKeyOutBackground_GradedBorderIsNotBorderKeyed(t *testing.T) {
+	img := image.NewNRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 16, 16))
+	// (210,60,210): distance to testMagenta (255,0,255) is

+	// so every pixel is flood-reachable but none is close enough to inner to

+	if d <= testInner || d >= testOuter {
+		t.Fatalf("test construction error: gradedBand distance %.1f is not strictly inside (inner=%.0f, outer=%.0f)",

+	}
+	for y := 0; y < 16; y++ {
+		for x := 0; x < 16; x++ {

+		}
+	}
+
+	out, stats := KeyOutBackground(img, testMagenta, testInner, testOuter)
+
+	if stats.BorderKeyed > 0.05 {
+		t.Fatalf("graded-band border (distance %.1f, reachable but never fully transparent): "+

+			"transparent read as BorderKeyed=1.000)", d, stats.BorderKeyed)
+	}
+	// Confirm the image genuinely is NOT transparent at its border — the
+	// assertion above is only meaningful if this is true.
+	if a := out.NRGBAAt(0, 0).A; a == 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("test construction error: corner (0,0) is fully transparent (alpha 0), " +
+			"so this is not actually testing the graded-not-transparent case")

keyground.go (pre-fix, this repo's own history at commit b2322a203): MatteStats.BorderKeyed's doc comment read 'the fraction (0..1) of the image's outermost ring of pixels that ended up fully transparent' while the computation used `keyedByBorder[idx(x,y)]` (BFS-reachability boolean) with no reference to final alpha -- confirmed by direct code read before writing this fix, not assumed from the report alone.

This session's own mutation proof (not committed): reinstating the pre-fix computation and running TestKeyOutBackground_GradedBorderIsNotBorderKeyed produces 'want BorderKeyed near 0, got 1.000' -- reproducing the live-reported number pattern exactly.
plan.risks: Low risk, narrow change: alters only how one float64 statistic is computed from data already being produced by the existing grading pass; does not change which pixels are keyed, how despill works, or the threshold check that consumes the stat. All prior keyground_test.go cases re-verified passing unchanged after this fix (10 pre-existing tests plus the 1 new one). The separately-reported despill-fringe issue (a residual magenta tint at the graded band on an otherwise-successful real generation) is NOT addressed by this commit -- recorded as a follow-up in docs024_key_docs_latest/bugfix_424_logo_transparency/NOTES_logo_transparency.md, not chased without the actual reported image to inspect.
